facts.fact: Tom Allen and Jem Mace agreed in January 1870 to a fight for the championship, and articles were drawn up.
facts.conflict: stake and title: $2,500 a side and the championship of America (286.c3, 286.c5) vs $10,000 and the championship of the world (228.c1, retro; 379.c6 also says world); signing date Jan 17 (228.c1) vs articles reaching the Clipper Jan 3 (286.c2)

facts.fact: Tom Allen declined Joe Coburn's January 1870 challenge to fight for $5,000 or $10,000, saying he would not fight Coburn until after his contest with Jem Mace, expected in July 1870.
Jem Mace wrote in a March 1870 card that he would only whip Tom Allen for the reputation and battle-money of their meeting, with no international character.
In May 1870 Tom Allen challenged all professional bruisers except Mace and Heenan to fight him, and was particularly anxious that Joe Coburn accept.
A match between Tom Allen and Jem Mace was set for July 5, 1870, to be fought within fifty miles of Cincinnati for $2,500 a side.
facts.conflict: date: a match to be fought near Cincinnati next March (378.c1, published Dec 1869) vs July 5, 1870 (286.c4, 379.c5); place: Cincinnati area (286.c4) vs a place the OCR garbles (379.c5)

facts.fact: Tom Allen and Mike McCoole were matched for the championship in summer 1870 with $1,000 deposited, but the second deposit was not paid.
facts.conflict: Allen's acceptance: he would not accept McCoole's last challenge (412.c1, July 9) vs a match to be contested (409.c3, June; 410.c6, $5,000 a side); 411.c3 says the second $500 deposit was not paid on July 1 and Roach claimed the stakes already deposited

facts.fact: Allen said no match had been made with Joe Goss, dismissing New York rumours of a $1,000-a-side match as moonshine.
In July 1870 Tom Allen sent the New York Clipper a challenge to fight any man in America for $2,500 or $5,000 a side, Joe Coburn preferred.

Tom Allen and James C. Gallagher signed articles at Hennessy's saloon on September 19, 1870 for a $1,500 match, with deposits paid through October. In November Gallagher proposed Louisiana, Kansas, Arkansas or Kentucky as the venue, and Allen said he would fight in any of them.
Jack Leoney offered $5,000 to back Tom Allen in a match in 1871.
In a letter dated January 1871 from St. Louis, Tom Allen said he had challenged Joe Coburn ten times and that Coburn never answered.
Allen offered Joe Coburn $200 to withdraw from his match with Jem Mace, and offered to stake $3,000 for a fight with Coburn on April 11, 1871, about fifty miles from Detroit.
A New York dispatch of May 14, 1871 said Tom Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn or Ned O'Baldwin, and Allen denied the dispatch on May 16.
facts.conflict: amounts: Coburn at $5,000 (431.c1, printed $5020; 432.c1) and O'Baldwin at $1,000 a side (431.c1) vs $1,090 (432.c1); Allen's denial (433.c1) vs the dispatch (431.c1, 432.c1)

facts.fact: In early 1872 Tom Allen and Mike McCoole were negotiating a match, with Billy Carroll offering to back McCoole and Allen putting up $500 to meet him.
facts.conflict: date: McCoole was reported to want a match in December 1871 (444.c1) vs a challenge made in 1872 (235.c12, retro)

facts.fact: A match between Tom Kelly and Tom Allen was rumoured in late November 1872, with friends of Kelly offering $500 or more to back him if Allen could be brought down to Kelly's weight.
